page: Microsoft Azure D64ps_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on 64-bit ARM architecture and managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is configured with 64 dedicated virtual CPUs and 256 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 4 GB allocated per core. It operates without hardware GPU accelerators and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Storage architecture for the D64ps_v7 is entirely remote-dependent, as the virtual machine contains no bundled local disk storage. High-throughput data access and persistence require network-attached storage, with the system providing support for Azure Premium Storage. The absence of local solid-state drives requires workloads to rely on external managed disks for both system OS volumes and scratch space.

From an efficiency perspective, the ARM64 platform delivers high core density and power-efficient parallel throughput compared to traditional compute platforms. However, operational tradeoffs include the absence of x86 vector extensions and the total reliance on remote storage latency for disk operations. This profile fits large-scale ARM-native application deployments, containerized microservices, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and web backend tiers.
description: Microsoft Azure D64ps_v7 is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the 64-bit ARM processor architecture and provisioned via Microsoft Hyper-V. The system integrates 64 dedicated vCPUs and 256 GB of system memory, matching a balanced allocation of 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include integrated local disk storage, operating as a diskless compute node that relies on network-attached Premium Storage for persistent file and block storage. Additionally, the instance contains zero GPUs and provides no complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Because of its ARM64 foundation, workloads must support ARM instructions, precluding the use of x86-specific hardware extensions. The configuration suits scalable multi-threaded workloads, container orchestration nodes, backend web services, and continuous integration runners requiring uniform memory-to-core ratios across a large number of dedicated cores without local NVMe dependencies.
